sources.title: 49.5MW solar farm approved on Grey Belt land near Cobham - Landmark Chambers
paragraphs: A planning inspector has granted planning permission for a 49.5MW ground-mounted solar photovoltaic array on approximately 52 hectares of agricultural land east of Cobham Road, Bookham, following a five-day public inquiry held in Pippbrook, Dorking in early 2026.

Mole Valley District Council had initially refused planning permission in April 2025 on grounds relating to landscape character, heritage settings, and Green Belt policy, overturning planning officers' recommendations to approve.

The inspector concluded that the site constitutes 'Grey Belt' under revised National Planning Policy Framework provisions and assigned very substantial weight to the renewable energy generation, energy security, and the utilisation of available electrical grid capacity.

sources.title: Fetcham : Solar farm approved – East Surrey News - Leatherhead Living
paragraphs: A government planning inspector has allowed the appeal for a commercial solar farm on land east of Cobham Road, Fetcham (MO/2024/1048), reversing the refusal issued by Mole Valley District Council.

The appeal inquiry, conducted in the Council Chamber at Pippbrook in Dorking, heard representations from local resident associations and energy developers regarding landscape visual impact, greenfield use, and local power needs.

sources.title: Solar Farm Application in Leigh - Leigh Parish Council
paragraphs: A planning application (MO/2024/1823) was submitted to Mole Valley District Council for an 11.32 MVA ground-mounted solar farm at Little Flanchford Farm, Flanchford Road, Leigh, near Dorking.

The scheme spans approximately 15 hectares (37 acres) for an operational duration of 40 years, with capacity to supply renewable electricity for up to 5,500 homes alongside supporting substation and inverter equipment.

sources.title: Ashtead Common Trustees Object to Installation of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)
paragraphs: The City of London Corporation, trustees of Ashtead Common, lodged formal objections with Mole Valley District Council regarding application MO/2024/1544 for a utility battery energy storage system (BESS) on land northwest of Barnett Wood Lane.

The conservation body raised concerns regarding the proximity to the Epsom and Ashtead Commons Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and National Nature Reserve, citing risks to biodiversity, hydrology, and fire management.
The major BESS development was ultimately approved with conditions by Mole Valley District Council in late 2025, with subsequent 2026 filings covering design variations and condition compliance.
